uncertainties: Only two refunding sources were read; interim statements between them were not checked, and bill versus coupon shares were not measured. The 2025 refunding is described from news commentary, which is not treated as an event. The Mandate's text says 50-year treasury bill; the record calls it a bond, the usual term for that maturity. Unchanged guidance is a non-action and is listed only to show status. Checked systematically on 2026-10-18: Federal Register API searches (Treasury-only and all agencies) found no document on longer-duration issuance or a 50-year security; the Unified Agenda listing was unreachable and the Fiscal Service proposed-rule listing held only the buyback rule (proposed 2026-01-14, final 2026-03-30), which concerns redemption operations and does not change issuance; one congress.gov and govinfo search found no related bill; the Treasury refunding page and press releases showed no change; and news searches showed unchanged coupon guidance. The August 2026 statement says financing needs beyond the steady coupon sizes are met with weekly bill auctions and notes growing private demand for bills, and Bloomberg reporting of November 2025 said bill auction sizes had reached record levels and the bill share was above 21 percent in September 2025; this tilt toward shorter debt runs against the recommendation but is not a stated policy, so the record stays not_started rather than diverged. Interim statements were not checked and the bill share was not measured from Treasury data; the next refunding falls after this check.
